title: Ford confirms talks with Max Verstappen about future Le Mans appearance
content:
SPA-FRANCORCHAMPS, Belgium — Ford has spoken with Max Verstappen about making a future appearance at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, which it believes could be possible while he is still racing in Formula 1.

Verstappen, 28, has won four F1 world championships, but has shown increasing levels of interest in sports car racing in recent years, including the formation of his own team.

The Dutchman will make his debut in the 24-hour race at the Nürburgring next weekend, and has previously spoken of a desire to race at Le Mans and fight for the overall win.

Ford returned to F1 in 2026 in collaboration with Red Bull for a brand-new engine program. In 2027, it will return to the top category of sports car racing, known as Hypercar, with a two-car entry to the World Endurance Championship (WEC) that includes Le Mans.

The relationship between Red Bull and Ford may open the door for Verstappen to potentially race one of its Hypercars in the future.

Speaking to reporters ahead of Saturday’s 6 Hours of Spa-Francorchamps WEC race, Mark Rushbrook, the global director of Ford Racing, said he “would love to see that, yes.”

“But a lot of things need to align for that to happen,” Rushbrook added. “Of course, that would be incredible for us, for the sport. We would love to see that.”

Rushbrook then confirmed there had been discussions with Verstappen about driving for Ford at Le Mans in the future, but said it was “not for 2027.”

Verstappen is currently under contract with Red Bull in F1 through to the end of 2028, but revealed at the end of March he was giving thought to his future in the series given his frustration with the all-new cars for 2026 and how they drive.

Although Rushbrook ruled out 2027, he said he thought Verstappen could make a Le Mans appearance while still racing in F1 “depending on the schedules and what’s going on.”

The last active F1 driver to race at Le Mans was Fernando Alonso in 2018, who won that year’s edition of the endurance classic for Toyota. Nico Hulkenberg also took victory at Le Mans in 2015 with Porsche while racing full-time in F1.

Asked about Verstappen’s reaction to the talks, Rushbrook said that “those discussions go back three-plus years,” dating back to when Ford’s partnership with Red Bull was first announced.

“It’s just looking for the right opportunity for things to align,” Rushbrook said, adding that Verstappen seemed interested in “with the right program, yeah.”

On Friday, F1’s governing body, the FIA, announced plans to make some changes to the design of the engines from 2027, moving away from the near-50/50 split between combustion and electrical power and move it closer to a 60/40 split.

Many drivers have expressed concerns about the reliance of the new cars on electrical power this year, which has led to less flat-out laps in qualifying and some unintuitive approaches in races to recharge the battery.

“It’s stakeholders voicing their opinions, decision-makers making their decisions,” said Rushbrook. “But I think that is a good step to help the racing and the product on the track.”

Verstappen and Red Bull have endured a difficult start to the new F1 season, failing to finish a race any higher than fifth through the opening four races.

But the performance of the new Red Bull Ford engine has been widely praised, given the project did not exist a few years ago and is now competing against manufacturers such as Ferrari and Mercedes that have decades of F1 experience.

Rushbrook said Red Bull and Ford had achieved many of their early goals at the start of 2026, but “want to continue working toward the very top” in F1.

“That’s what everyone wants, to be able to win races and championships,” said Rushbrook. “We know it’s going to take a lot of work to get there. That’s part of why we partnered with Red Bull. They are racers, they’re committed to winning.

“Last year, what they showed, they were in a deficit, and they clawed back within two points of getting the championship for Max. We know it’s the right partner.

“We’re fully committed for all of our resources going to help that program.”
